module_title: Rejection of Plaint, Inherent Powers, and Appellate Mechanisms
introduction: Tailored for advanced legal exams, corporate litigators, and UPSC Law Optional, this level explores the absolute powers of the civil court, the strict grounds for throwing out a case before trial, and the technical hierarchy of Reference, Review, and Revision.

core_concepts.title: Rejection of Plaint (Order 7 Rule 11)
core_concepts.description:
A lethal weapon used by defendants to kill a suit at the threshold.
- Grounds for Rejection: The court SHALL reject the plaint if: (a) It does not disclose a cause of action, (b) The relief claimed is undervalued (and plaintiff fails to correct it), (c) Plaint is insufficiently stamped, or (d) The suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be **barred by any law** (e.g., barred by the Limitation Act).
- Return vs Rejection: Return of plaint (O7 R10) happens when the court lacks territorial or pecuniary jurisdiction (plaintiff takes it to the correct court). Rejection (O7 R11) means the suit is legally flawed and dismissed.

core_concepts.title: Inherent Powers of the Court (Section 151)
core_concepts.description:
The ultimate safety net of the CPC.
- The Rule: Nothing in this Code shall be deemed to limit or otherwise affect the inherent power of the Court to make such orders as may be necessary for the **ends of justice** or to **prevent abuse of the process of the Court**.
- Limitation: Inherent powers cannot be used if there is an express provision in the CPC dealing with the matter. They supplement the code, they do not override it.

core_concepts.title: Temporary Injunctions (Order 39)
core_concepts.description:
A judicial order restraining a party from doing a particular act until the final disposal of the suit (to preserve the status quo/property in dispute).
- Granting Criteria: The plaintiff must prove three things: (1) A *Prima Facie* case in their favor, (2) Balance of Convenience is in their favor, and (3) They will suffer Irreparable Injury if the injunction is not granted.

core_concepts.title: Reference (Sec 113), Review (Sec 114) & Revision (Sec 115)
core_concepts.description:
The 3 R's of Appellate mechanisms:
- Reference (Sec 113): A subordinate court refers a pending case to the High Court if it involves a question on the validity of an Act/Ordinance.
- Review (Sec 114): A party applies to the **SAME judge** who passed the decree to reconsider it, based on the discovery of new/important evidence or an error apparent on the face of the record.
- Revision (Sec 115): The High Court calls for the record of a case decided by a subordinate court where no appeal lies, to check if the lower court exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction, or acted with material irregularity.

important_entities.name: Caveat (Section 148A)
important_entities.key_fact: A preemptive warning to the court.
important_entities.significance: A 'Caveat' is a notice filed by a person anticipating that an application may be made against them in a suit. It ensures that the court will not pass any ex-parte order against the Caveator without giving them a prior notice and a hearing. A caveat remains valid for **90 days**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Advanced exams heavily test Section 100 (Second Appeal). Can you file a Second Appeal to the High Court because you believe the lower court misunderstood the facts or evidence? **NO**. A Second Appeal under Section 100 lies to the High Court ONLY on a **Substantial Question of Law**. Factual findings of the First Appellate Court are final.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Reference = To High Court (Law validity); Review = To Same Judge (Error); Revision = To High Court (Jurisdictional error)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use this quick mapping to distinguish the three post-decree/pending mechanisms.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Law Optional, when discussing the power of civil courts to render substantive justice outside procedural loopholes, anchor your argument on **Section 151 (Inherent Powers)**, highlighting it as the 'equitable soul' of the rigid procedural code.
